title: Which weather year sets the hydrogen store of a zero-emission German power system, and how much does the cost depend on it?
summary: Re-solves energy-mix-sourced (one-node PyPSA model, solar, onshore wind, gas, Li-ion and hydrogen storage, PyPSA technology-data 2030 costs in 2025 euros) on five weather and demand years of Open Power System Data / ENTSO-E (2015 to 2019) instead of only 2019; 20 deterministic LPs. At zero emissions the cost ranges EUR 203 to 271/MWh with a steel hydrogen tank (2018 cheapest, 2017 and 2015 dearest) and EUR 141 to 155 with caverns, so the tank case moves by about EUR 68 between years and the cavern case by about EUR 14. The hydrogen store is set by the year: 1.1 to 5.6 TWh with a tank (2015 largest) and 23.7 to 35.9 TWh with caverns (2016 largest), against 24.9 TWh in 2019 alone; the tank case needs 1.0 to 1.7 TWh of batteries. At a 95% cut the tank case buys no hydrogen in any year and costs EUR 118 to 133. The 2019 results reproduce the sibling project (EUR 222 and 144). Limitations: five years, each solved separately with perfect foresight (a store sized for all five years together was not solved), one node, no imports or offshore wind, capacity factors from actual generation so they include curtailment, caverns not sited or limited, and the 7% discount rate is not from a source.
lede: which weather year sets the hydrogen store of a zero-emission German power system? The same sourced-cost PyPSA model on 2015 to 2019: EUR 203 to 271/MWh with a steel tank, EUR 141 to 155 with caverns, and a cavern store of 24 to 36 TWh depending on the year.
